verses.21:5: Joab gave the number of the enrollment of the people to David. In all Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and in Judah there were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.21:6: But he did not enroll Levi and Benjamin among them, because the word of the king was abhorrent to Joab.
verses.21:7: This thing was evil in the eyes of God, and He struck Israel.
verses.21:8: David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in doing this thing. Now, please remove the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
verses.21:9: Then the LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,
verses.21:10: "Go and speak to David, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: I am holding out three things before you; choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you.'"
verses.21:11: So Gad came to David and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Take for yourself,
verses.21:12: either three years of famine, or three months of being swept away before your foes while the sword of your enemies overtakes you, or three days of the sword of the LORD and pestilence in the land, with the angel of the LORD bringing destruction throughout all the territory of Israel.' Now see what word I should return to Him who sent me."
verses.21:13: David said to Gad, "I am in severe distress. Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, because His mercies are exceedingly great, and into the hand of man let me not fall."
verses.21:14: Then the LORD sent pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men from Israel fell.
verses.21:15: And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it; but as he was destroying, the LORD looked and relented over the calamity, and He said to the destroying angel, "Enough! Now let your hand drop." Now the angel of the LORD was standing beside the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:16: David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between the earth and the heavens, with his drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, covered in sackcloth, fell down on their faces.
verses.21:17: David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people to be counted? Indeed, I am the one who has sinned and done great evil. But these sheep, what have they done? LORD my God, please let Your hand be against me and against my father's house, and not against Your people to bring a plague."
verses.21:18: Then the angel of the LORD instructed Gad to tell David that David should go up to erect an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:19: So David went up at Gad's word, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.
verses.21:20: Now Ornan turned around and saw the angel, and his four sons with him hid themselves, while Ornan was threshing wheat.
verses.21:21: When David came up to Ornan, Ornan looked out and saw David, and he went out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.
verses.21:22: Then David said to Ornan, "Give me the place of the threshing floor so that I may build an altar to the LORD on it. Give it to me for the full price, so that the plague may be restrained from the people."
verses.21:23: Ornan said to David, "Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good in his eyes. Look, I give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering; I give it all."
verses.21:24: But King David said to Ornan, "No, for I will surely buy it for the full price. I will not take what belongs to you for the LORD, nor offer up a burnt offering without cost."
verses.21:25: So David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the place.
verses.21:26: David built an altar to the LORD there and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings. And he called to the LORD, and He answered him with fire from the heavens upon the altar of burnt offering.
verses.21:27: Then the LORD commanded the angel, and he returned his sword to its sheath.
verses.21:28: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
verses.21:29: For the tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
verses.21:30: Yet David was unable to go before it to inquire of God, because he was terrified by the sword of the angel of the LORD.
verses.22:1: Then David said, "This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar for burnt offering for Israel."
verses.22:2: David gave orders to gather the resident foreigners who were in the land of Israel, and he appointed stonecutters to quarry dressed stones for building the house of God.
verses.22:3: David also prepared iron in abundance for the nails of the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and bronze in abundance beyond weighing,
verses.22:4: and cedar timbers beyond number, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought cedar timbers in abundance to David.
verses.22:5: David said, "Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly grand, for renown and splendor throughout all the lands; I will now prepare for it." So David prepared in abundance before his death.
verses.22:6: Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.22:7: David said to Solomon, "My son, as for me, it was in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.
verses.22:8: But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed blood in abundance and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for My name, because you have shed much blood on the ground before Me.
verses.22:9: Look, a son will be born to you; he shall be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. For Solomon shall be his name, and I will grant peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
verses.22:10: He is the one who will build a house for My name, and he will be a son to Me, and I will be a father to him; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
verses.22:11: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, so that you may succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, just as He has spoken concerning you.
verses.22:12: Only may the LORD grant you insight and understanding, and appoint you over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
verses.22:13: Then you will succeed if you take care to carry out the statutes and the ordinances that the LORD commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and resolute; do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed.
verses.22:14: Now look, in my hardship I have prepared for the house of the LORD one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, because it is in such abundance. I have also prepared wood and stones, and you may add to them.
verses.22:15: Furthermore, you have workers in abundance: stonecutters, craftsmen of stone and wood, and every person skilled in every kind of work.
verses.22:16: Of the gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and act, and may the LORD be with you."
verses.22:17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son:
verses.22:18: "Is not the LORD your God with you, and has He not given you rest on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before the LORD and before His people.
verses.22:19: Now give your heart and your soul to seeking the LORD your God. Arise and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the name of the LORD."
verses.23:1: Now David was old and full of days, and he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
verses.23:2: And he gathered all the officials of Israel, and the priests and the Levites.
verses.23:3: The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward, and their number, head by head among the men, was thirty-eight thousand.
verses.23:4: "Of these, twenty-four thousand are to supervise the work of the house of the LORD, and six thousand are officers and judges,
verses.23:5: and four thousand are gatekeepers, and four thousand are praising the LORD with the instruments that I made for giving praise."
verses.23:6: And David divided them into divisions by the sons of Levi, for Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.23:7: Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
verses.23:8: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the head, and Zetham, and Joel, three.
verses.23:9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to Ladan.
verses.23:10: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei, four.
verses.23:11: Jahath was the head, and Zizah was the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they became a father's house for one enrollment.
verses.23:12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.
verses.23:13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart so that he would consecrate the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to Him, and to bless in His name forever.
verses.23:14: Now as for Moses, the man of God, his sons were named under the tribe of Levi.
verses.23:15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
verses.23:16: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the head.
verses.23:17: And the sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the head; Eliezer had no other sons, yet the sons of Rehabiah grew exceedingly numerous.
verses.23:18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the head.
verses.23:19: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the head, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
verses.23:20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the head and Isshiah the second.
verses.23:21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
verses.23:22: Eleazar died and had no sons, only daughters; so the sons of Kish, their relatives, took them as wives.
verses.23:23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.
verses.23:24: These were the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, the heads of the fathers' houses according to their enrollment, by the count of names, head by head, who did the work for the service of the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and upward.
verses.23:25: For David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has granted rest to His people, and He dwells in Jerusalem forever.
verses.23:26: And furthermore, the Levites need not carry the tabernacle or any of its vessels for its service."
verses.23:27: For according to the final words of David, these were the numbered sons of Levi from twenty years old and upward.
verses.23:28: For their station was at the side of the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD, over the courts and over the chambers, and over the purification of every holy thing, and the work of the service of the house of God,
verses.23:29: and for the bread of the rows, and for the fine flour for a grain offering, and for the unleavened wafers, and for what is cooked on a griddle, and for what is well-mixed, and for every measure of volume and size;
verses.23:30: and to stand morning by morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise at evening;
verses.23:31: and at every offering of burnt offerings to the LORD, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and at the appointed feasts, by the number according to the ordinance required of them, continually before the LORD.
verses.23:32: So they were to keep the charge of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the sons of Aaron, their brothers, for the service of the house of the LORD.
verses.24:1: Now concerning the sons of Aaron, their divisions: the sons of Aaron were Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.24:2: Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar ministered as priests.
verses.24:3: And David, along with Zadok from the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their assigned order in their service.
verses.24:4: Now the sons of Eleazar were found to be more numerous in male heads than the sons of Ithamar, so they divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen heads of fathers' houses, and for the sons of Ithamar, eight by their fathers' houses.
verses.24:5: They divided them by lots, the one with the other, for there were officials of the sanctuary and officials of God from the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.
verses.24:6: Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, from the Levites, recorded them in the presence of the king and the officials, and Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites: one father's house taken for Eleazar, and taken in turn for Ithamar.
verses.24:7: The first lot came out for Jehoiarib; for Jedaiah, the second;
verses.24:8: for Harim, the third; for Seorim, the fourth;
verses.24:9: for Malchijah, the fifth; for Mijamin, the sixth;
verses.24:10: for Hakkoz, the seventh; for Abijah, the eighth;
verses.24:11: for Jeshua, the ninth; for Shecaniah, the tenth;
verses.24:12: for Eliashib, the eleventh; for Jakim, the twelfth;
verses.24:13: for Huppah, the thirteenth; for Jeshebeab, the fourteenth;
verses.24:14: for Bilgah, the fifteenth; for Immer, the sixteenth;
verses.24:15: for Hezir, the seventeenth; for Happizzez, the eighteenth;
verses.24:16: for Pethahiah, the nineteenth; for Jehezkel, the twentieth;
verses.24:17: for Jachin, the twenty-first; for Gamul, the twenty-second;
verses.24:18: for Delaiah, the twenty-third; for Maaziah, the twenty-fourth.
verses.24:19: This was their assigned order for their service, to come into the house of the LORD according to their ordinance by the hand of Aaron their father, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
verses.24:20: Now concerning the remaining sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
verses.24:21: Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the head.
verses.24:22: Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
verses.24:23: And the sons: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
verses.24:24: The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
verses.24:25: The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
verses.24:26: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Jaaziah his son.
verses.24:27: The sons of Merari, of Jaaziah his son: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
verses.24:28: Of Mahli: Eleazar, and he had no sons.
verses.24:29: Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
verses.24:30: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites by their fathers' houses.
verses.24:31: They also cast lots just like their brothers, the sons of Aaron, in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites, the head of the fathers' house just like his younger brother.
verses.25:1: David and the commanders of the army separated for the service the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, harps, and cymbals. And the number of them, the men of work for their service, was:
verses.25:2: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the direction of the king.
verses.25:3: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun with the lyre, who prophesied in thanking and praising the LORD.
verses.25:4: Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
verses.25:5: All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer in the words of God, to lift up a horn; and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
verses.25:6: All these were under the direction of their father for singing in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman were under the direction of the king.
verses.25:7: And the number of them along with their brothers who were trained in singing to the LORD, all who were skilled, was two hundred eighty-eight.
verses.25:8: And they cast lots for their duties equally, the small just like the great, teacher together with student.
verses.25:9: The first lot came out for Asaph, for Joseph. The second was for Gedaliah; he and his brothers and his sons were twelve.
verses.25:10: The third was for Zaccur; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:11: The fourth was for Izri; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:12: The fifth was for Nethaniah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:13: The sixth was for Bukkiah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:14: The seventh was for Jesarelah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:15: The eighth was for Jeshaiah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:16: The ninth was for Mattaniah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:17: The tenth was for Shimei; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:18: The eleventh was for Azarel; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:19: The twelfth was for Hashabiah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:20: The thirteenth was for Shubael; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:21: The fourteenth was for Mattithiah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:22: The fifteenth was for Jeremoth; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:23: The sixteenth was for Hananiah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:24: The seventeenth was for Joshbekashah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:25: The eighteenth was for Hanani; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:26: The nineteenth was for Mallothi; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:27: The twentieth was for Eliathah; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:28: The twenty-first was for Hothir; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:29: The twenty-second was for Giddalti; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:30: The twenty-third was for Mahazioth; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.25:31: The twenty-fourth was for Romamti-ezer; his sons and his brothers were twelve.
verses.26:1: For the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, from the sons of Asaph.
verses.26:2: And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
verses.26:3: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
verses.26:4: And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
verses.26:5: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth, because God blessed him.
verses.26:6: And to his son Shemaiah sons were born who were rulers over their father's house, because they were mighty men of ability.
verses.26:7: The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, and his brothers, men of ability: Elihu and Semachiah.
verses.26:8: All these were from the sons of Obed-edom; they and their sons and their brothers were men of ability with strength for the service, sixty-two belonging to Obed-edom.
verses.26:9: And Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, men of ability, eighteen.
verses.26:10: And Hosah, from the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri was the head; though he was not the firstborn, his father made him head.
verses.26:11: Hilkiah was the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
verses.26:12: To these divisions of the gatekeepers, to the head men, belonged duties corresponding to their brothers, to minister in the house of the LORD.
verses.26:13: And they cast lots, the small just like the great, according to their fathers' houses, for each gate.
verses.26:14: The lot to the east fell to Shelemiah. And for his son Zechariah, a counselor with insight, they cast lots, and his lot came out to the north.
verses.26:15: For Obed-edom, to the south; and for his sons, the house of the storehouses.
verses.26:16: For Shuppim and for Hosah, to the west, with the Gate of Shallecheth on the ascending highway, watch corresponding to watch.
verses.26:17: On the east there were six Levites, on the north four each day, on the south four each day, and at the storehouses two by two.
verses.26:18: For the Parbar on the west, four were at the highway and two at the Parbar.
verses.26:19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers of the sons of the Korahites and of the sons of Merari.
verses.26:20: As for the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasuries of the house of God and over the treasuries of the dedicated things.
verses.26:21: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites of Ladan, the heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
verses.26:22: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and Joel his brother were over the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
verses.26:23: Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
verses.26:24: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries.
verses.26:25: And his brothers through Eliezer were Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.
verses.26:26: This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things that King David, the heads of the fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the commanders of the army had dedicated.
verses.26:27: From the wars and from the plunder they dedicated them to maintain the house of the LORD.
verses.26:28: And all that Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated—whatever anyone had dedicated was under the charge of Shelomith and his brothers.
verses.26:29: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outside work over Israel, as officers and judges.
verses.26:30: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of ability, were over the administration of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
verses.26:31: Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was the head of the Hebronites according to their generations by fathers' houses. In the fortieth year of David's reign they were sought out, and mighty men of ability were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.
verses.26:32: And his brothers, men of ability, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers' houses; and King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter of God and every matter of the king.
verses.27:1: Now the sons of Israel according to their number—the heads of the fathers' houses, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter of the divisions coming in and going out month by month for all the months of the year—each division was twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:2: Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:3: He was from the sons of Perez, the chief of all the commanders of the armies for the first month.
verses.27:4: Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and of his division Mikloth was the leader; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:5: The third commander of the army for the third month was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:6: This is the Benaiah who was a mighty man of the Thirty and over the Thirty, and over his division was Ammizabad his son.
verses.27:7: The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:8: The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:9: The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:10: The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:11: The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:12: The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:13: The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:14: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, from the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:15: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:16: Now over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer the son of Zichri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
verses.27:17: for Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
verses.27:18: for Judah, Elihu, one of the brothers of David; for Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
verses.27:19: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;
verses.27:20: for the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
verses.27:21: for the half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
verses.27:22: for Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the chiefs of the tribes of Israel.
verses.27:23: Now David did not take a count of those twenty years old and under, because the LORD had promised to multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.
verses.27:24: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to count, but did not finish; and wrath came upon Israel because of this, and the number was not entered in the account of the chronicles of King David.
verses.27:25: Over the treasuries of the king was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah.
verses.27:26: Over those who did the work of the field for tilling the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub.
verses.27:27: Over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over what was in the vineyards for the storehouses of wine was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
verses.27:28: Over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the storehouses of oil was Joash.
verses.27:29: Over the cattle grazing in Sharon was Shirtai the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai.
verses.27:30: Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the female donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
verses.27:31: Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials of the property belonging to King David.
verses.27:32: Now Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the sons of the king.
verses.27:33: Ahithophel was counselor to the king, and Hushai the Archite was the friend of the king.
verses.27:34: After Ahithophel came Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar; and the commander of the king's army was Joab.
verses.28:1: Then David assembled to Jerusalem all the officials of Israel: the chiefs of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions who served the king, the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, and the officials over all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, along with the court officers, the mighty men, and every mighty man of valor.
verses.28:2: Then King David rose to his feet and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. As for me, it was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations to build.
verses.28:3: Yet God said to me, 'You are not to build a house for My name, for you are a man of wars and have shed blood.'
verses.28:4: Still, the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of all my father's house to be king over Israel forever; for He chose Judah as leader, and in the house of Judah, my father's house, and among my father's sons He was pleased with me, to make me king over all Israel.
verses.28:5: And out of all my sons—for the LORD has given me many sons—He chose my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
verses.28:6: And He said to me, 'Your son Solomon is the one who will build My house and My courts, for I have chosen him for Myself as a son, and I Myself will be a father to him.
verses.28:7: And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he remains strong to carry out My commandments and My judgments, as on this day.'
verses.28:8: So now, before the eyes of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek all the commandments of the LORD your God, in order that you may possess the good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your sons after you forever.
verses.28:9: And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul, because the LORD searches all hearts and discerns every inclination of the thoughts. If you seek Him, He will let Himself be found by you; yet if you abandon Him, He will cast you off forever.
verses.28:10: See now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary; be strong and act."
verses.28:11: Then David gave his son Solomon the pattern of the vestibule and its buildings, its storerooms, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and the room of the atonement cover,
verses.28:12: and the pattern of all that he had in the spirit: for the courts of the house of the LORD, and for all the surrounding chambers, for the treasuries of the house of God and for the treasuries of the consecrated things;
verses.28:13: also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of the service of the house of the LORD;
verses.28:14: for the golden things, by weight of gold, for all the articles of every kind of service; and for all the silver articles by weight, for all the articles of every kind of service;
verses.28:15: and the weight for the lampstands of gold and their lamps of gold, by the weight of each lampstand and its lamps, and for the lampstands of silver by weight, for a lampstand and its lamps, according to the service of each lampstand;
verses.28:16: and the gold by weight for the tables of the arranged bread, for each table, and silver for the tables of silver;
verses.28:17: and the forks, the basins, and the pitchers of pure gold; and for the golden bowls by weight for each bowl, and for the silver bowls by weight for each bowl;
verses.28:18: and for the altar of incense, refined gold by weight; and for the pattern of the chariot—the golden cherubim spreading out their wings and covering over the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
verses.28:19: "All this, in writing from the hand of the LORD upon me, He made clear—all the works of the pattern."
verses.28:20: And David said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and courageous, and act. Do not be afraid and do not be terrified, because the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not let go of you or abandon you until all the work of the service of the house of the LORD is completed.
verses.28:21: And here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God, and with you in all the work is every willing person with skill for every kind of service, as well as the officials and all the people for all your commands."
verses.29:1: Then King David said to the whole assembly, "Solomon my son, the only one whom God has chosen, is young and tender, and the work is great, because the palace is not for a human being, but for the LORD God.
verses.29:2: Now with all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God: the gold for the gold articles, the silver for the silver, the bronze for the bronze, the iron for the iron, and the wood for the wood; onyx stones and stones for setting, antimony stones and variegated stones, every precious stone, and marble stones in abundance.
verses.29:3: Furthermore, because of my delight in the house of my God, the private treasure of gold and silver that belongs to me I have given to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house:
verses.29:4: three thousand talents of gold, from the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the buildings,
verses.29:5: gold for the gold articles and silver for the silver, and for all work by the hand of craftsmen. Now who offers willingly to fill his hand today for the LORD?"
verses.29:6: Then the leaders of the fathers' houses, the leaders of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials of the king's work offered willingly.
verses.29:7: And they gave for the service of the house of God: gold, five thousand talents and ten thousand darics; silver, ten thousand talents; bronze, eighteen thousand talents; and iron, one hundred thousand talents.
verses.29:8: And any with whom stones were found gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
verses.29:9: Then the people rejoiced over their willing offering, because with a whole heart they had offered willingly to the LORD; and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
verses.29:10: Then David blessed the LORD before the eyes of the whole assembly, and David said, "Blessed are You, LORD, God of Israel our father, from eternity and to eternity.
verses.29:11: Yours, LORD, are the greatness, the might, the glory, the eminence, and the majesty, because everything in the heavens and on the earth belongs to You; Yours, LORD, is the kingdom, and You are the One exalted as head over all.
verses.29:12: Wealth and honor come from Your presence, and You rule over all. In Your hand are strength and might, and it is in Your hand to make great and to strengthen all.
verses.29:13: And now, our God, we are giving thanks to You and praising Your glorious name.
verses.29:14: Yet who am I, and who are my people, that we should possess strength to offer willingly like this? For everything is from You, and out of Your hand we have given to You.
verses.29:15: For we are sojourners before You and temporary residents, like all our fathers; like a shadow are our days on the earth, and there is no hope.
verses.29:16: LORD our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build for You a house for Your holy name is from Your hand, and everything belongs to You.
verses.29:17: And I know, my God, that You examine the heart and delight in uprightness; as for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things, and now I have seen with joy Your people who are found here offering willingly to You.
verses.29:18: LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel our fathers, keep this forever in the inclination of the thoughts of Your people's heart, and establish their heart toward You.
verses.29:19: And to my son Solomon give a whole heart to keep Your commandments, Your testimonies, and Your statutes, and to do everything, and to build the palace for which I have prepared."
verses.29:20: Then David said to the whole assembly, "Now bless the LORD your God." So the whole assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed low and prostrated themselves before the LORD and before the king.
verses.29:21: And they offered sacrifices to the LORD and brought up burnt offerings to the LORD on the day after that day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
verses.29:22: They ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great joy. And a second time they made Solomon son of David king, and they anointed him for the LORD as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
verses.29:23: So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David; he prospered, and all Israel heeded him.
verses.29:24: And all the officials and the mighty men, as well as all the sons of King David, gave their hand under King Solomon.
verses.29:25: And the LORD made Solomon exceedingly great before the eyes of all Israel, and bestowed on him royal majesty such as had not been on any king before him over Israel.
verses.29:26: And David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
verses.29:27: And the days that he reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three.
verses.29:28: Then he died at a good old age, full of days, wealth, and honor; and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
verses.29:29: Now the deeds of King David, first and last—see, they are written in the records of Samuel the seer, and in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the records of Gad the seer,
verses.29:30: together with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

notes.1:7: The Masoretic Text reads Tarshishah (with a final -ah ending, compared with Tarshish in Genesis 10:4) and Rodanim (compared with Dodanim in Genesis 10:4).
notes.1:32: The Hebrew opens with a genealogical heading ("And the sons of Keturah, concubine of Abraham") and shifts directly into the finite Qal verb "she gave birth to" followed by the direct object marker.
notes.1:42: The Masoretic Text reads Dishon here (matching verse 41), whereas verse 38 and Genesis 36:28 spell the seventh son of Seir as Dishan.
notes.1:46: Ketiv/Qere: the written consonantal text transposes the middle letters (yod before vav), whereas the read form (qere) translated here is Avith, matching Genesis 36:35.
notes.1:51: Ketiv/Qere: the written consonantal text reads Aliah, whereas the read form (qere) translated here is Alvah, matching Genesis 36:40. The noun rendered "chieftain" translates Hebrew alluph, a tribal or clan leader, standing without the definite article before each clan or district name.
notes.2:3: Bath-shua can also be rendered 'the daughter of Shua' (cf. Gen 38:2, 12); the Niphal verb rendered 'were born' is masculine singular with the collective numeral 'three.'
notes.2:18: The Hebrew syntax is difficult, literally reading 'fathered [particle] Azubah a wife and [particle] Jerioth'; understanding the particle as the preposition 'with' yields the sense of fathering children with them.
notes.2:24: The Masoretic Text reads the place name 'in Caleb-ephrathah' and introduces the main clause with the conjunction before 'Hezron's wife Abijah'; the Septuagint reflects a different consonantal reading ('Caleb went in to Ephrathah').
notes.2:50: The Masoretic Text reads singular 'the son of Hur' (presenting a later Caleb who was Hur's son, whose sons follow in vv. 50b-51), whereas the Septuagint and Vulgate read plural 'The sons of Hur' to begin a new clause.
notes.2:55: Ketiv/qere variant: the qere (translated here) reads the Qal active participle construct 'living at' (yoshve), whereas the ketiv has consonants pointing to a finite verb ('they lived').
notes.3:2: The Hebrew prefixes the preposition le- to Absalom, functioning here as an emphatic or itemizing marker typical of Late Biblical Hebrew lists rather than a preposition of parentage.
notes.3:17: Masoretic accentuation connects assir with Jeconiah as an epithet, 'Jeconiah the captive'; alternatively, it may be read as a personal name, 'Assir, with Shealtiel his son.'
notes.3:21: The Masoretic text repeats the plural construct 'sons of' four times here, introducing four Davidic family lines without specifying their generational link to Hananiah.
notes.3:22: The Masoretic text gives the total 'six' while naming five sons of Shemaiah, either counting Shemaiah together with his five sons or reflecting a name not preserved in the list.
notes.3:24: Ketiv writes a variant orthography (hwdywhw), while Qere reads Hodavyahu ('Hodaviah').
notes.4:3: The Masoretic text literally reads 'and these, the father of Etam' (avi Etam), keeping the singular title 'father of' rather than 'sons of.'
notes.4:7: Ketiv writes ytzhr ('Izhar' or 'Jezohar') without a conjunction, while Qere reads ve-Tzohar ('and Zohar').
notes.4:10: Hebrew im introduces an optative wish ('If only'), ve-asita me-ra'ah is an elliptical idiom literally meaning 'and You would act away from harm,' and otzbi ('cause me pain') plays on the name Jabez and the noun 'pain' in 4:9.
notes.4:17: The feminine verb 'and she conceived' (va-tahar) refers to an unnamed wife in this verse who is identified at the end of 4:18 as Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.
notes.4:20: Ketiv writes wtwlwn ('and Tolon'), while Qere reads ve-Tilon ('and Tilon').
notes.4:41: Ketiv writes hm'ynym with yod, while Qere reads ha-Me'unim ('the Meunites').
notes.5:1: The Hebrew clause וְלֹא לְהִתְיַחֵשׂ לַבְּכֹרָה uses the Hithpael infinitive construct of יחשׂ ("to be registered by genealogy") with negative לֹא to indicate that the genealogical order did not follow the birthright.
notes.5:6: The Masoretic Text of Chronicles spells this Assyrian king's name Tilgath-pilneser (also in 5:26 and 2 Chronicles 28:20), corresponding to Tiglath-pileser in 2 Kings 15:29.
notes.5:20: The form וְנַעְתּוֹר is a Niphal infinitive absolute of עתר functioning as a finite verb continuing the preceding clause, conveying that God let Himself be moved and responded favorably to their plea.
notes.5:26: Pul was the Babylonian throne name of Tilgath-pilneser (Tiglath-pileser III), and the following singular Hiphil verb וַיַּגְלֵם ("and he carried them into exile") treats them as one ruler, using a proleptic object suffix specified by the Late Biblical Hebrew direct-object preposition לְ.
notes.5:27: Verses 5:27–41 in the Masoretic Hebrew versification correspond to 1 Chronicles 6:1–15 in most English translations.
notes.6:11: The Hebrew Qere reads 'sons of' (bene), translated here, whereas the Ketiv has 'his son' (beno).
notes.6:13: The Masoretic Text reads 'the firstborn Vashni, and Abijah,' omitting Joel (cf. 6:18; 1 Samuel 8:2); 'Vashni' is widely thought to reflect 'and the second' after the name Joel dropped out.
notes.6:16: 'Stationed' renders the Hiphil of amad ('cause to stand,' hence appoint or station), echoing the Qal forms of the same root in 6:17, 18, and 24. 'Over the direction of song' translates the Hebrew idiom al-yede-shir, literally 'over the hands of song.'
notes.6:20: The Hebrew Qere reads 'Zuph' (tsuf, matching 1 Samuel 1:1), translated here, whereas the Ketiv has 'Ziph' (tsif).
notes.6:33: 'Were given' renders the Qal passive participle of natan ('give,' netunim), reflecting the Levites' dedication to sanctuary service as in Numbers 3:9 and 8:16.
notes.6:34: 'Burned offerings' translates the Hiphil participle of qatar ('turn into smoke'), a term covering both animal sacrifices on the altar of burnt offering and incense on the altar of incense.
notes.6:42: The Hebrew text uses the plural 'cities of refuge' (are hammiqlat) here and in 6:52, even though only Hebron (here) and Shechem (in 6:52) were designated cities of refuge in these lists (cf. Joshua 21:13, 21).
notes.6:43: The Masoretic Text here reads 'Hilez' (with final zayin), whereas many Hebrew manuscripts and editions read 'Hilen' (cf. Holon in Joshua 21:15).
notes.6:46: The Hebrew text reads literally 'from the clan of the tribe, from the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh,' repeating 'half' with two synonyms (machatsit and chatsi) and omitting the names of Ephraim and Dan (cf. 6:51-55; Joshua 21:5).
notes.7:1: Following the qere Jashub; the ketiv writes Jashib.
notes.7:10: Following the qere Jeush; the ketiv writes Jeish.
notes.7:14: The Masoretic pausal accent divides the verse after 'whom she bore,' leaving Asriel's mother unnamed before introducing Manasseh's Aramean concubine as the mother of Machir; some take the concubine as the subject of both verbs.
notes.7:23: The name Beriah plays on the Hebrew phrase bera'ah, 'in calamity,' where the preposition 'in' is retained before the noun for the sake of the wordplay.
notes.7:31: Following the qere Birzaith; the ketiv writes Birzoth.
notes.7:34: Following the qere forms Rohgah and Hubbah; the ketiv spells Rohgah with a vowel letter waw and writes Jehubbah without the conjunction 'and.'
notes.7:35: Hebrew literally reads the singular 'son of Helem' before listing four sons, likely used collectively or as an abbreviated form of 'sons of.'
notes.8:6: The Hiphil verb in "they exiled them" is third-person masculine plural and may function as an impersonal passive ("they were exiled"). Verse 7 then uses the same Hiphil root in the singular ("it was he who exiled them"), referring to Gera, with the initial conjunction on Naaman resuming the list of Ehud's sons.
notes.8:8: The Hiphil verb "fathered" is used absolutely here without an expressed direct object ("children" is supplied for English). "After he had sent them away" renders a temporal preposition with the Piel infinitive construct of shalach ("send away," here divorce) and a masculine plural suffix referring to his two wives.
notes.8:25: Ketiv/Qere: the written consonantal text (ketiv) reads "Peniel," while the traditional reading (qere) translated here is "Penuel."
notes.8:29: The verb "lived" is plural before the singular subject "the father of Gibeon," likely referring collectively to him and his household. Unlike the parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9:35, the Masoretic Text here does not include the personal name Jeiel.
notes.8:38: The Masoretic vocalization points "Bocheru" as a proper name rather than "his firstborn," which matches the stated total of six sons.
notes.9:4: Translates the qere min-benei, meaning 'from the sons of'; the ketiv has transposed consonants spelling Binyamin ('Benjamin') before Perez.
notes.9:17: The Masoretic Text vocalizes achihem as singular ('their brother') and joins it by accentuation to Shallum, though some understand it collectively as 'their relatives; Shallum was the chief.'
notes.9:22: Hebrew emunah literally means 'faithfulness' and is used here and in vv. 26 and 31 for a permanent position of trust or entrusted charge.
notes.9:33: Translates the qere peturim, the Qal passive participle of patar ('exempt' or 'released'); the ketiv writes the variant form petirim with the same sense.
notes.9:35: Translates the qere Yeiel ('Jeiel'); the ketiv writes Yeuel ('Jeuel').
notes.9:41: The Masoretic Text lists three sons of Micah here without naming Ahaz, who introduces the next generation in v. 42.
notes.10:3: Hebrew wayyachel is a Qal wayyiqtol of chul/chil ('writhe in pain' or 'tremble in anguish'); in context the anguish may imply that he was wounded.
notes.10:12: Hebrew elah denotes a terebinth tree rather than the tamarisk in the parallel account of 1 Samuel 31:13, and gufah ('body' or 'corpse') appears in Biblical Hebrew only in this verse.
notes.10:13: The infinitive lishol ('to consult' or 'ask') plays on the name Saul (Shaul) from the same root, while lidrosh ('to make inquiry') contrasts directly with v. 14 ('did not inquire of the LORD').
notes.11:8: Hebrew yechayyeh is the Piel of chayah ("keep alive" or "revive"), used idiomatically here for restoring or rebuilding a ruined city.
notes.11:11: Following the Qere ("the captains" or "the officers," hash-shalishim, plural of shalish); the Ketiv reads "the thirty" (hash-sheloshim).
notes.11:20: Following the Qere ("and he had a name"); the Ketiv writes the negative particle ("and not"). The Masoretic Text reads "the three" in both clauses of this verse.
notes.11:21: Hebrew bash-shenayim ("doubly") literally reads "by the two" or "among the two," a compressed expression distinguishing Abishai's rank from the premier Three.
notes.11:22: Hebrew shene ari'el mo'av literally reads "two Ariels of Moab" (from ari, "lion," and el, "God" or "mighty"), likely denoting two famed lion-like champions of Moab.
notes.12:3: Ketiv/Qere: the qere reads we-Yiziel ("and Jeziel"), whereas the ketiv writes a form corresponding to "and Jezuel."
notes.12:6: Ketiv/Qere: the qere reads ha-Charufi ("the Haruphite"), whereas the ketiv writes a form corresponding to "the Hariphite."
notes.12:15: Hebrew echad le-me'ah ha-qatan we-ha-gadol le-alef ("lit. one to a hundred the least, and the greatest to a thousand") can denote either martial prowess (a match for a hundred or a thousand) or rank (commanding a hundred or a thousand).
notes.12:19: Ketiv/Qere: the qere reads ha-shalishim ("the officers"), whereas the ketiv writes ha-sheloshim ("the thirty"). Also, the Qal verb laveshah literally means "clothed"; here ruach stands without "of God" or "of the LORD" (contrast Judg 6:34; 2 Chr 24:20).
notes.12:34: The rare Qal infinitive construct la'ador means to keep battle rank (as in 12:39, oderei ma'arakhah), though some connect it with an Aramaizing form of "help"; Hebrew be-lo lev wa-lev is literally "without a heart and a heart," meaning undivided loyalty.
notes.13:2: Hebrew nifretsah nishlechah joins two Qal cohortatives asyndetically ("let us break out, let us send") to express sending word far and wide; the root p-r-ts ("break out") recurs as a motif in 13:11 and 14:11.
notes.13:6: The Masoretic clause asher-niqra shem ("which is called by the Name," Niphal perfect 3ms of qara) is elliptical, lacking a pronominal suffix or preposition (unlike the fuller parallel in 2 Sam 6:2).
notes.13:12: The interrogative hekh ("How?") is a late Biblical Hebrew form of ekh attested only here and in Daniel 10:17.
notes.14:1: Ketiv/Qere: the qere reads Churam ("Huram"), whereas the ketiv writes Chiram ("Hiram," as in 2 Sam 5:11).
notes.14:2: The Niphal feminine singular participle nisse't (from nasa, "lift up") functions predicatively with the feminine subject malkhuto ("his kingdom") to express its exalted state.
notes.14:14: Hebrew ha-bekha'im refers to a kind of tree whose exact botanical identity is uncertain; "balsam trees" is a probable identification.
notes.15:12: Hebrew el-hakinoti lo attaches the definite article as a relative marker to the Hiphil perfect verb ("to [the place] that I have prepared for it"), an elliptical Late Biblical Hebrew construction omitting the antecedent noun "place."
notes.15:13: Hebrew lemabbarishonah is a rare compound preposition-adverb meaning "at the first time," followed by the elliptical clause lo attem ("not you," i.e., you were not the ones carrying the ark).
notes.15:20: Alamoth (literally "young women" or "maidens") and the Sheminith in 15:21 (literally "the eighth") are Hebrew musical terms of uncertain technical meaning, likely indicating pitch registers, tunings, or musical modes (compare the superscriptions of Psalms 6, 12, and 46).
notes.15:22: Hebrew massa ("lifting up") can denote either carrying the ark or lifting the voice in music/singing (compare 15:27, where it is paired with "the singers"); yasor is the Qal infinitive absolute of yasar, here used for instructing or directing.
notes.15:24: Ketiv reads the quadriliteral denominative participle mhtstsrim ("trumpeting," from chatsotserah, "trumpet"), whereas Qere reads the Hiphil participle machtserim from the shortened triliteral root chtsr; both mean "blowing trumpets."
notes.16:3: The exact meaning of the rare Hebrew noun eshpar (occurring only here and in 2 Samuel 6:19) is uncertain; it is traditionally rendered "a portion of meat," though some scholars propose "a date cake" in parallel with "raisin cake."
notes.16:15: The Masoretic text of 1 Chronicles 16:15 reads the Qal imperative zikru ("Remember!"), whereas the parallel in Psalm 105:8 reads the Qal perfect zakar ("He remembers").
notes.16:19: The Masoretic text reads the second-person plural suffix bihyotekem ("When you were"), shifting to third-person plural in 16:20; the parallel in Psalm 105:12 reads third-person plural ("When they were").
notes.16:36: Hebrew wehallel is the Piel infinitive absolute of halal continuing the preceding finite verb ("and praised the LORD"), a characteristic Late Biblical Hebrew construction.
notes.16:42: The Masoretic text places "Heman and Jeduthun" in apposition to the pronoun suffix on "with them" ("with them—Heman and Jeduthun—were trumpets and cymbals..."), rather than omitting the two names as in the Septuagint.
notes.17:5: Hebrew reads literally "from tent to tent and from a tabernacle" (u-mi-mishkan), an elliptical expression parallel to "from tent to tent" implying "from one tabernacle to another."
notes.17:9: The verb le-valloto is the Piel infinitive construct of balah ("to wear out, waste away"), distinctive to Chronicles (compare 2 Samuel 7:10, "to afflict").
notes.17:17: The Hebrew clause u-re'itani ke-tor ha-'adam ha-ma'alah is syntactically obscure, literally "and You have looked upon me according to the order/rank of the man, the ascent/high degree," rendered here following the Qal vocalization of ra'ah ("looked upon").
notes.17:18: Hebrew le-khavod 'et-'avdekha uses the noun kavod ("honor") with a direct object marker ('et), functioning verbally like an infinitive ("for honoring Your servant").
notes.17:25: Hebrew matsa' 'avdekha uses matsa' ("found") absolutely without an explicit direct object, idiomatically meaning "found boldness/courage" to pray.
notes.18:3: Hebrew le-hatstiv yado (Hiphil of natsav + yad) reads literally "to set up his hand," an idiom meaning either "to establish his dominion" or "to erect his victory monument."
notes.18:6: The Masoretic Hebrew reads literally "and David stationed in Aram of Damascus," omitting an explicit direct object; "garrisons" (netsivim) is supplied from the parallel wording in 18:13.
notes.18:10: Ketiv/Qere orthographic variant: the ketiv writes lsh'wl (plene) and the qere reads lish'ol-lo (defective spelling with maqqef); both represent the Qal infinitive construct of sha'al ("to inquire").
notes.18:16: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "Abimelech" here (compare "Ahimelech" in 2 Samuel 8:17 and 1 Chronicles 24:3, 6, 31).
notes.19:4: Hebrew ha-mifsa'ah is a biblical hapax legomenon from the root pasa' ("to stride, step"), denoting the fork of the legs, i.e., the hips or crotch.
notes.19:6: Hebrew hitba'ashu is the Hithpael of ba'ash ("to stink"), literally "made themselves a stench," i.e., thoroughly offensive.
notes.19:13: Hebrew chazaq we-nitchazzeqah pairs the Qal imperative ("be strong") with the Hithpael cohortative ("let us prove ourselves strong") of the root chazaq.
notes.19:18: Hebrew rekhev (literally "chariots, chariotry") here denotes chariot crews ("charioteers") as the direct object of the verb "killed" (harag).
notes.20:2: Hebrew malkam means "their king," though the same consonants can also be vocalized as Milcom (or Malcam), the national deity of the Ammonites.
notes.20:3: The rare Qal verb wayyasar ("and he cut" or "sawed") differs from the parallel in 2 Samuel 12:31, which reads wayyasem ("and he set"). The Masoretic Text also repeats "with saws" (bamgerot) at the end of the list, where 2 Samuel 12:31 reads "with axes."
notes.20:4: Hebrew ha-repha'im ("the Rephaim") is plural here, whereas 20:6 and 20:8 use the singular with the definite article, ha-rapha ("Rapha" or "the Rephaite"), denoting a lineage of giant warriors.
notes.20:5: Ketiv reads "Jaor" (or "Jaur"); Qere reads "Jair" (ya'ir), which is translated here.
notes.21:1: Hebrew satan appears here without the definite article and may be understood either as the proper name "Satan" or as the common noun "an adversary."
notes.21:12: The form le-masseghet combines the preposition le- with a Hiphil feminine singular participle of nasag ("to overtake"), a Late Biblical Hebrew predicative construction agreeing with the feminine noun "sword."
notes.21:17: The paired forms hare'a hare'oti combine the Hiphil infinitive absolute and Hiphil perfect of ra'a' for intensive emphasis ("done great evil").
notes.21:30: Hebrew lephanaw ("before it") refers back to the tabernacle and altar of burnt offering at Gibeon mentioned in 21:29.
notes.22:7: Ketiv reads "his son" (beno), closing the narrative introduction; Qere reads "My son" (beni), opening David's address to Solomon, and is translated here.
notes.22:9: The name Solomon (Shelomoh) plays on shalom ("peace") in the following clause, reinforcing the theme of "rest" (menuchah) and "give rest" (hanichoti, Hiphil of nuach).
notes.22:14: Hebrew be'onyi literally means "in my affliction" or "in my hardship," expressing the great pains and difficult circumstances under which David gathered these provisions.
notes.23:5: The Hebrew shifts abruptly into first-person speech with the Qal perfect verb עָשִׂיתִי ("I made") without an explicit introductory speech verb, indicating that the allocation in verses 4-5 is presented as David's own decree.
notes.23:9: Following the qere שְׁלֹמִית ("Shelomith"); the ketiv reads שלמות ("Shelomoth", as in 1 Chronicles 24:22). Note also that verse 10 spells the son of Shimei as Zina (זִינָא), whereas verse 11 spells the same name Zizah (זִיזָה).
notes.23:13: The third-person suffix on the Hiphil infinitive לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ is grammatically ambiguous: it is translated here as subjective ("so that he would consecrate the most holy things"), though it can also be construed as objective ("to consecrate him as most holy").
notes.23:27: Literally "they were the number of the sons of Levi"; the pronoun הֵמָּה ("they") functions copulatively to identify the Levites enrolled from twenty years old and upward under David's final directive.
notes.24:6: The Masoretic Text literally reads וְאָחֻז ׀ אָחֻז לְאִיתָמָר ("and taken, taken for Ithamar"), repeating the Qal passive participle of אחז with a Masoretic paseq; this is rendered distributively ("taken in turn"), whereas ancient versions reflect "and one taken for Ithamar."
notes.24:23: The Masoretic Text reads literally וּבְנָי יְרִיָּהוּ ("And the sons: Jeriah"), with a disjunctive accent separating וּבְנָי from יְרִיָּהוּ and omitting both "Hebron" and "the head" that appear in the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 23:19.
notes.24:24: Following the qere שָׁמִיר ("Shamir"); the ketiv reads שמור ("Shamur").
notes.24:26: In both verses 26 and 27, Masoretic conjunctive accents and the spirantized form בְנוֹ bind the word directly to יַעֲזִיָּהוּ as "Jaaziah his son," though some interpreters treat בְנוֹ as a proper name ("Beno") because of the conjunction on וְשֹׁהַם ("and Shoham") in verse 27.
notes.24:31: The phrase אָבוֹת הָרֹאשׁ (literally "the fathers of the head") is an inverted idiomatic expression for the senior head of a fathers' house, placed on equal footing in the casting of lots with his younger brother.
notes.25:1: Ketiv reads the plural noun 'the prophets,' while the translated Qere reads the Niphal participle 'who prophesied' (compare vv. 2-3).
notes.25:3: The Masoretic Hebrew lists five sons of Jeduthun here before the total 'six'; the sixth son, Shimei, appears in the lot list at v. 17.
notes.25:5: 'To lift up a horn' (Hiphil infinitive construct of rum with qeren) is a Hebrew idiom for exalting honor or strength, though some understand it literally of sounding a horn.
notes.25:8: 'Teacher' renders the Hiphil participle mebin (one who imparts understanding or is skilled), paired with talmid ('student'), which occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.25:9: The Masoretic Hebrew omits the tally phrase ('he and his sons and his brothers, twelve') after Joseph, stating it only for Gedaliah.
notes.26:6: 'Who were rulers' renders the plural of the noun mimshal ('dominion' or 'rule'), used concretely here for rulers.
notes.26:18: 'The Parbar' transliterates the rare Hebrew term happarbar (likely a loanword), referring to a colonnade, annex, or western precinct of the temple.
notes.26:20: The Masoretic Hebrew reads the personal name 'Ahijah' after the topical heading 'As for the Levites,' rather than 'their brothers' as in the Septuagint.
notes.26:25: Ketiv reads 'Shelomoth' (matching the spelling in v. 26), while the translated Qere reads 'Shelomith' (matching v. 28).
notes.26:28: 'All that ... had dedicated' uses the definite article ha- as a relative pronoun before the Hiphil perfect verb hiqdish (a Late Biblical Hebrew feature), and 'whatever anyone had dedicated' renders the Hiphil participle hammaqdish used elliptically.
notes.27:2: Hebrew 'al machaluqto (lit. "upon his division") is a Late Biblical Hebrew idiom meaning "in" or "assigned to his division," recurring across the monthly roster in vv. 2-15.
notes.27:5: In Hebrew hakkohen rosh, rosh ("chief/head") lacks the definite article and is separated from hakkohen ("the priest") by a disjunctive accent, allowing either "the son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief" (describing Benaiah) or "the son of Jehoiada the chief priest."
notes.27:12: The Ketiv writes one word ("of the Benjaminite"), whereas the Qere divides it into two words (labben yemini, the older two-word gentilic form); both denote the tribe of Benjamin.
notes.27:24: The Qal verb 'alah ("went up") is used in the archival sense "was entered/recorded," and the Masoretic Text reads bemispar ("in the account/enumeration") rather than besefer ("in the book").
notes.27:29: Translates the Qere Shirtai; the Ketiv reads Shitrai.
notes.28:9: Hebrew yimmatse lakh is the Niphal tolerative of matsa ("He will let Himself be found by you"), and the verb root darash ("searches" / "seek") directly echoes "seek" in v. 8.
notes.28:12: Hebrew baruach ("in the spirit") carries the definite article and can be understood either of the divine Spirit (compare v. 19) or of David's own spirit, i.e., "in mind."
notes.28:18: Hebrew hammerkabah ("the chariot") stands in apposition to "the golden cherubim," and "their wings" is implied with the Qal participle leforesim ("spreading out," cf. Exod 25:20).
notes.28:19: The Masoretic Text shifts abruptly to first-person speech ('alay, "upon me") without an introductory speech formula; hiskil is the Hiphil of sakal ("made clear" or "gave understanding of").
notes.29:5: Hebrew "fill his hand" (Piel infinitive construct of male with "hand") is an idiom for dedicating oneself or bringing a consecrated offering to the LORD (compare Exodus 32:29).
notes.29:11: Hebrew netsach, translated "eminence," denotes surpassing splendor, enduring preeminence, or triumph. The Hithpael participle hammithnasse ("the One exalted") attributes supreme exaltation to the LORD as head over all.
notes.29:16: Ketiv/Qere: the written consonantal text (Ketiv) has the feminine singular pronoun hi, while the traditional reading (Qere) has the masculine singular pronoun hu, agreeing with the masculine singular antecedent "abundance" (hamon).
notes.29:24: Hebrew "gave their hand under King Solomon" (literally "gave a hand under") is a formal idiom for pledging allegiance and submitting to royal authority.
notes.29:29: Hebrew uses two distinct prophetic titles here translated "seer": Samuel is called haro'eh (Qal participle of ra'ah, "to see"), while Gad is called hachozeh (Qal participle of chazah, "to behold in vision").
